items.title: Wayne Bergeron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 29, 2020
items.q: I want John Lewis for first trumpet on the classical stuff and I want Wayne for the commercial stuff

ctx.x: Was it, is it possible to not be all in with studio work? Like let’s say you got to a point, you wanted to cut back a little bit so I’m not going to accept any Saturday dates or whatever. Is it possible to do that or do you find that if you’re trying to step out a little bit that you’re going to end up stepping out completely?

If you did it a lot — but I think that most of the people I work for, because I always look at like there’s contractors and there’s composers and there’s orchestrators. And the orchestrators and the composers are actually more powerful than the contractors. Because many of them will have their list of musicians that they like, or, depending on the kind of music it is who they want there. So I have composers that I work for that are always going to have me on their list. It’s going to say Wayne Bergeron first…
